ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a horizontal ground, and above the ground is fixed a vertically placed semicircular smooth track. The lower end of the semicircular track is near the ground, and the upper end is directly above it; the small block is near the lower end of the track, and an arrow indicates that it slides into the track with horizontal speed v, and afterward can fly out horizontally from the upper end of the track. Reasoning: The track is smooth, so mechanical energy is conserved during the process in which the small block rises along the track from the lower end to the upper end. The diameter of the semicircle is vertical, so the height difference from the lower end to the upper end is 2R. Let the speed of the small block when it reaches the upper end be u, then (1/2)mv^2=(1/2)mu^2+mg·2R, so u^2=v^2-4gR. The small block flies out horizontally from the upper end, and the height from which it flies out is 2R. The initial velocity in the vertical direction is 0, so the time to land satisfies 2R=(1/2)gt^2, giving t=2√(R/g). Since the upper end of the track is directly above the lower end, the horizontal distance from the landing point to the lower end of the track is x=ut. Thus x^2=u^2t^2=(v^2-4gR)·4R/g=4R(v^2-4gR)/g. To make the distance x maximum, it is only necessary to make x^2 maximum. Regard it as a quadratic function of R: x^2=4Rv^2/g-16R^2. Its opening is downward, and the maximum value corresponds to the vertex: d(x^2)/dR=4v^2/g-32R=0, solving gives R=v^2/(8g).

raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure there is a horizontal ground, and above the ground is fixed a vertically placed semicircular smooth track. The lower end of the semicircular track is near the ground, and the upper end is directly above it; the small block is near the lower end of the track, and an arrow indicates that it slides into the track with horizontal speed v, and afterward can fly out horizontally from the upper end of the track.

Reasoning: The track is smooth, so mechanical energy is conserved during the process in which the small block rises along the track from the lower end to the upper end. The diameter of the semicircle is vertical, so the height difference from the lower end to the upper end is 2R. Let the speed of the small block when it reaches the upper end be u, then
(1/2)mv^2=(1/2)mu^2+mg·2R,
so u^2=v^2-4gR.

The small block flies out horizontally from the upper end, and the height from which it flies out is 2R. The initial velocity in the vertical direction is 0, so the time to land satisfies
2R=(1/2)gt^2,
giving t=2√(R/g).

Since the upper end of the track is directly above the lower end, the horizontal distance from the landing point to the lower end of the track is
x=ut.
Thus
x^2=u^2t^2=(v^2-4gR)·4R/g=4R(v^2-4gR)/g.

To make the distance x maximum, it is only necessary to make x^2 maximum. Regard it as a quadratic function of R:
x^2=4Rv^2/g-16R^2.
Its opening is downward, and the maximum value corresponds to the vertex:
d(x^2)/dR=4v^2/g-32R=0,
solving gives R=v^2/(8g).
